Ethical platforms to use instead of Etsy. Here are 7 ethical alternatives people are switching to. Artisans Cooperative. Owned by its makers and shoppers, one vote per member, with the community verifying shops are handmade. Folksy. It bans resellers and mass-produced imports, and makers get paid directly. Handfair. One owner, no investors, makers keep 100% of the item price, and it blocks AI from training on their work. Mayhem Marketplace. It charges a flat subscription instead of taking a cut of every sale, and it bans dropshipping and products made mainly by AI. Marmalade. A small team that checks the handmade shops it promotes. No AI, no dropshipping. Big Cartel. Independent since 2005, no commission, and a free plan. Wolf & Badger. A certified B Corp marketplace where every brand is owned by its designer. Starting December 16, Etsy and its partners can use sellers' photos and descriptions to train AI. Sellers can't just turn it off in their settings. Artists are already pulling their shops. Over the years, Etsy started allowing factory-made goods, went public, dropped its B Corp certification, and now answers to shareholders before its users. Buyers say the site is filled with junk. Etsy is rated a D on the Conscious Spend app, where we are on a mission to show consumers how ethical almost any company is so people can find ethical alternatives to evil corporations. You can also use the app to see who owns what you buy, better alternatives, and the ethics score, and join over 125k people using it to spend for a better world.

Those top sellers on Etsy have some things in common 👀 I’ve been selling on Etsy for 6 years and I’ll be honest with you, there isn’t a magic formula. Anyone who tells you otherwise, is probably trying to sell you something. BUT!! there are things I see top Etsy sellers do over and over again that I believe 100% helps them make more sales: 1) They use DATA. This is a big one that so many new sellers overlook. Top sellers aren’t just randomly deciding what niche they want to sell in or what phrase to put on their shirt. They use tools like Everbee, erank, or RankHero to find profitable niches BEFORE they put a single product in their Etsy shop. They also use these tools to optimize their titles, tags, and general SEO. Stop guessing, start using DATA 🙌 2) They study design trends. Top sellers have their finger on the pulse of what is currently trending. They use Pinterest, other Etsy shops, trends reports, and just in general their eyes and minds when they are out shopping to start noticing patterns of what is currently trending and then they apply those trends to their designs! 🥳 3) They use Print on Demand. Not all of them, but most of the top shops I see are using Printify as their supplier so that they can sell more products! 🙌 When you can test out different designs and styles and products without the upfront costs, you are giving yourself so many more chances to be found by your target audience. Print on demand is a game changer for Etsy sellers and I talk a LOT about how you can use Printify in your Etsy shop! 💖 4) Their mockups are on POINT. This is something I will never stop shouting from the rooftops because it is THAT important. Good mockups can make or break your Etsy shop - get some good ones!! 5) They don’t give up!! They test and test and test and take any data and information they get and apply it to more designs, more products, and that eventually leads to more sales. Keep learning, keep growing, and don’t give up because YOU CAN DO THIS!! And if you have any questions I’m always here to help!! 💖💖 #etsyseller #etsytips #printondemand #etsytipsandtricks #etsyforbeginners Etsy tips for beginners. Start Etsy in 2026.
